summary.text: Cynthia Soma-Hernandez is the Democratic candidate for the Maine House of Representatives, District 72, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces Republican Douglas Thomas.
A former teacher and railroad union officer, she has run for the Maine House in 2018 and 2024.

paragraphs.text: Soma-Hernandez graduated from Bulkeley High School, earned a bachelor's degree in sociology from the University of Connecticut in 1976 and a graduate degree from St. Peter's College in 1989.
Her career experience includes working at Amtrak and as an education advocate and teacher.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, she said she grew up in a family of nine children, entered the University of Connecticut on a full scholarship, and later worked as a railroad laborer and served her union as recording secretary and president.
She said she then taught for twenty-five years in Newark, New Jersey, and served as a national Sanders representative in 2016.
Soma-Hernandez ran for Maine House District 112 as a Democrat in 2018 and lost to incumbent Thomas Skolfield.
In 2024 she ran for District 72 as an independent and lost to Elizabeth Caruso, 27.6 percent to 72.4 percent.
She advanced from the Democratic primary for District 72 on June 9, 2026.
In the 2026 survey, Soma-Hernandez said her key messages include housing, education, food and medicine, more resources for seniors, and protecting job opportunities as technology changes work.
